outline.subject: Rainier Brewing Company was a Seattle-based company that produced a popular brand of beer in the Pacific Northwest.

sections.title: Rainier Brewing Company
sections.covers: This section introduces the company, its history in Seattle, its current ownership, and the status of its iconic brewery building and neon sign.

sections.title: Origins
sections.covers: This section details the early history of brewing in Seattle and the founding of the company that eventually produced Rainier beer.

sections.title: The Prohibition era
sections.covers: This section describes how the company navigated the prohibition of alcohol by producing nonalcoholic products and operating a brewery in another city.

sections.title: Post-Prohibition relaunch
sections.covers: This section covers the resumption of brewing operations after the repeal of Prohibition and the company's expansion under new ownership.

sections.title: Creative packaging
sections.covers: This section discusses the company's decorative beer can series and its extensive, surrealist advertising campaigns.

sections.title: Demise
sections.covers: This section outlines the sale of the company, the closure of the original brewery, and the subsequent changes in production and ownership.

sections.title: Rainier R logo
sections.covers: This section explains the history and evolution of the company's iconic red R logo and the neon sign atop the brewery.

sections.title: In popular culture
sections.covers: This section highlights various appearances and references to the beer in films, television, music, and news media.
